correctness.rationale: Before the first rejection, the published SAFFRON recursion keeps only the initial-wealth term. The index equals one plus the number of prior noncandidates. At stage \(j\), a rejection has probability \(a_j\), a nonrejecting candidate has probability \(\lambda-a_j\) and repeats the stage, and a noncandidate has probability \(1-\lambda\) and advances. Summing the geometric loop gives rejection-before-advance probability \(a_j/(1-\lambda+a_j)\), and multiplying stage survivals gives the exact product. In the uncapped case, elementary product and logarithm inequalities give the two-sided envelope. A fresh exact-rational finite-state replay independently matched the stage factorization on a finite schedule.
correctness.risk: The exact law is only for the first rejection under independent uniform nulls; after a rejection the reward terms enter, exactly as the result states.

value.rationale: The exact law separates the candidate-filtering clock from gamma allocation and quantifies the attained complete-null conservatism of a standard adaptive online FDR procedure. The sharp concentration/diffusion envelope is a motivated calibration boundary and provides exact implementation benchmarks, not merely a restatement of validity.
value.risk: The result concerns first rejection/global-null calibration only and does not claim a full rejection-count law.

final_claim: For constant-\(\lambda\) SAFFRON on an independent infinite complete-null stream, the first-rejection stage has the stated exact geometric-stage law, so the eventual complete-null FDR is \(1-\prod_j(1-\lambda)/(1-\lambda+a_j)\); in the uncapped regime this yields the stated sharp concentration/diffusion envelope.
limitations: The exact law assumes independent exactly uniform null p-values and the constant-lambda SAFFRON recursion.
It does not describe post-first-rejection counts, alternatives, dependence or time-varying candidate thresholds.
